thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INC IDENT: p95 latency spike on /v1/generate across hosted cluster us-west-2. Alert rule: api.latency.p95 > 3500ms for 3m. Paging oncall.
maria.sre: acked. I'm oncall. Initial customer impact: increased error budget burn and timeouts for several customers on medium traffic. Not yet seeing 5xx surge, mostly slow tail.
ajay.oncall: paging details: dropped user-facing throughput by ~20% and p95 went from ~400ms -> ~2.8s around 2026-03-15T05:22:00Z. p50 stable. Rolling deploy? any kernel or infra changes around ~05:20Z?
kevin.runtime: I can confirm p50 stayed ~200ms. p95 jump concentrated on nodes in pool-gpu-2 (nv4). Correlation with hosts that upgraded linux kernel to 6.8.1-rc last night (automated security rollout).
sarah.prodeng: oh that's a red flag. Did the rolling kernel job target only a subset? Which ASGs? any kube drains? link to rollout: https://internal/release/rollouts/2026-03-14/ker-6.8
maria.sre: copying a quick trace snippet from a high-p95 request (span IDs obfuscated):

```
span: proxy->model-runtime  0.2s
span: model-runtime->kernel-sched  2.5s  <-- huge
span: kernel-sched->gpu-queue  0.05s
```

kevin.runtime: that matches. We're seeing long scheduling latency inside kernel (sched_switch wait). Perf counters show increased context switch latency and involuntary preemption spikes on the upgraded hosts.
maria.sre: here's the perf stat from one affected host (abridged):

```
# perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations -I 1000 sleep 3
1000, 2026-03-15 05:23:00, 32000, 400
1001, 2026-03-15 05:23:01, 48000, 600
```

sarah.prodeng: do we have a quick mitigation? can we pin traffic away from affected ASGs for a few minutes? or fallback to smaller model-sized variant until we fix kernel?
ajay.oncall: I'm initiating mitigation: cordon and evict pods from nodes with kernel 6.8.1-rc in pool-gpu-2. Starting traffic reweight to dedicated-reserve pool. ETA 2m.

kevin.runtime: also enabling model fallback policy for hostnames with high tail latency (route to quantized-2 model which has slightly lower perf but cheaper queueing). Patching routing rules now.

maria.sre: deploy-bot: any recent runtime configuration changes?
deploy-bot: @maria.sre No runtime config deploys at 05:00-05:30Z. The only infra change was kernel automated rollout ID ker-2026-03-14-02.

kevin.runtime: hypothesis 1: kernel scheduler optimization in 6.8.1-rc interacts poorly with our GPU driver path, causing long sleeps before worker threads wake. Hypothesis 2: a change in IRQ affinity or softirq handling increased latency for the GPU submission thread on affected hosts.
sarah.prodeng: agreed. next steps for RCA: collect kernel release info, dmesg for any warnings, perf top captures and full tracing spans for affected requests. We should build a timeline: when kernel rollouts started, when p95 rose, and which hosts involved.

maria.sre: timeline so far:
- 2026-03-14T23:50Z: automated kernel rollout started (batch size 50 hosts)
- 2026-03-15T05:18Z: first affected host finished upgrade
- 2026-03-15T05:22Z: p95 spike observed
- 2026-03-15T05:25Z: mitigation: cordon and traffic reweight started
- 2026-03-15T05:31Z: p95 trending back down to ~600ms

ajay.oncall: customer impact notes: three customers reported timeouts, one has high-priority support case. Logged incident page: https://incidents.internal/2478004321

kevin.runtime: I'm collecting `perf record` and `bpftrace` captures now. Sharing a bpftrace snippet to snapshot scheduler events for pid X:

```
# bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:sched:sched_switch /pid == PID/ { printf("%s -> %s %d\\n", comm, args->next_comm, args->next_prio); }' > /tmp/sched-switch.log &
```

maria.sre: paste important dmesg lines here so we can see OOPS or warnings.
kevin.runtime: dmesg excerpt from node-74:

```
[May 15 05:21:47] watchdog: task model-worker blocked for 2487ms
[May 15 05:21:47] kernel: possible softirq overload
```

sarah.prodeng: good. For live RCA we should capture a set of affected hosts (5 samples) and an unaffected host (control) and compare perf metrics, trace spans, and dmesg. Kevin, can you upload artifacts to shared folder?

kevin.runtime: uploading to s3://redwood-incidents/2478004321/artifacts/ (perf.data, bpftrace.log, dmesg.txt). link: https://s3.internal/2478004321

maria.sre: tracking hypotheses in-thread:
- H1: kernel 6.8.1-rc scheduler regression interacting with GPU driver -> high p95 (supported by perf & bpftrace) [status: likely]
- H2: unrelated user workload spike causing queueing -> low (p50 stable, no new traffic to pool)
- H3: model runtime regression -> low (no runtime deploys)

ajay.oncall: mitigation status: cordon completed for 8 nodes; reweight completed for 3 minutes ago. p95 dropped from 2.8s -> 580ms. Removing pages to customers: support notified.

sarah.prodeng: next steps post-incident: rollback kernel rollout to previous stable kernel for affected ASGs and block automated kernel upgrades until further testing. Also run regression test with kernel-6.8-branch against our infra test harness.

maria.sre: assigning owners: kevin.runtime will lead kernel traces + artifact analysis (owner: kevin). sarah.prodeng will coordinate rollback and release blocking (owner: sarah). ajay.oncall will follow up with customer comms (owner: ajay).

kevin.runtime: quick note: I see a distinct code path in the scheduler where wait_for_completion_timeout is being used around gpu submission. I'll instrument and run a reproducer in staging with kernel 6.8.1-rc.

maria.sre: closing loop for now: incident de-escalated at 2026-03-15T05:40:00Z after p95 stabilized under 700ms. Keeping this thread for RCA artifact aggregation and postmortem.

sarah.prodeng: adding a follow-up: schedule a 1-hour RCA working session at 10:00Z today. Agenda: reproduce, perf diffs, rollback plan, customer note draft.

ajay.oncall: customer note draft (short):
"We detected increased tail latency impacting some requests between 05:22 and 05:35 UTC. Root cause: interaction between a recent kernel patch and our GPU workload; we've mitigated by routing traffic off impacted hosts and are rolling back the kernel rollout. No data loss and service fully restored." :thumbsup:

maria.sre: thanks team. attaching links to artifacts and timeline in the postmortem doc: https://docs.internal/rca/2478004321

incident-bot: Incident 2478004321: status=resolved severity=high. Metrics snapshot attached.
